const EPS = 1e-6;

function sweptHit(px, py, ball, brick) {
  const r = ball.r;
  const minX = brick.x - r;
  const maxX = brick.x + brick.w + r;
  const minY = brick.y - r;
  const maxY = brick.y + brick.h + r;
  const dx = ball.x - px;
  const dy = ball.y - py;

  let tmin = 0;
  let tmax = 1;
  let enter = null;   // { axis: 'x'|'y', value: 'min'|'max' }
  let corner = false;

  if (dx === 0) {
    if (px < minX || px > maxX) return null;
  } else {
    let t1 = (minX - px) / dx;
    let t2 = (maxX - px) / dx;
    if (t1 > t2) [t1, t2] = [t2, t1];
    if (t1 > tmin) {
      tmin = t1;
      enter = { axis: 'x', value: dx > 0 ? 'min' : 'max' };
      corner = false;
    } else if (Math.abs(t1 - tmin) <= EPS && t1 > 0) {
      corner = true;

    tmax = Math.min(tmax, t2);
    if (tmin > tmax) return null;

    let t2 = (maxY - py) / dy;

// --- Brick collision resolution (issue #1) --------------------------------

// Axis-aligned sweep of the ball (a circle, radius r) travelling from (px,py)
// to (ball.x, ball.y) against one brick. Returns the first contact as
// { t, x, y, face } or null:
//   t    – time of contact, 0 = already touching at the start of the step
//   x, y – contact position (ball centre)
//   face – one of 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | corner faces
//
// The brick is inflated by the ball radius (Minkowski sum): the moving centre
// vs. the inflated rectangle is a plain segment-vs-AABB test (slab method).
// This is what makes the detection tunnelling-proof: a fast ball whose centre
// jumps OVER a brick still crosses the inflated rectangle.
const EPS = 1e-6;

function sweptHit(px, py, ball, brick) {
  const r = ball.r;
  const minX = brick.x - r;
  const maxX = brick.x + brick.w + r;
  const minY = brick.y - r;
  const maxY = brick.y + brick.h + r;
  const dx = ball.x - px;
  const dy = ball.y - py;

  // Slab method: intersect the [0,1] parameter range with the interval of t
  // where the centre is inside the inflated rect, axis by axis.
  let tmin = 0;
  let tmax = 1;

  if (dx === 0) {
    if (px < minX || px > maxX) return null;
  } else {
    let t1 = (minX - px) / dx;
    let t2 = (maxX - px) / dx;
    if (t1 > t2) [t1, t2] = [t2, t1];
    tmin = Math.max(tmin, t1);
    tmax = Math.min(tmax, t2);
    if (tmin > tmax) return null;
  }

  if (dy === 0) {
    if (py < minY || py > maxY) return null;
  } else {
    let t1 = (minY - py) / dy;
    let t2 = (maxY - py) / dy;
    if (t1 > t2) [t1, t2] = [t2, t1];
    tmin = Math.max(tmin, t1);
    tmax = Math.min(tmax, t2);
    if (tmin > tmax) return null;
  }

  if (tmin > 1) return null;
  const t = Math.max(0, tmin);
  const x = px + (ball.x - px) * t;
  const y = py + (ball.y - py) * t;
  return { t, x, y, face: penetrationFaces(x, y, r, brick) };
}

// Which face(s) of the brick the ball at (cx,cy) penetrated. The face with the
// SMALLEST penetration depth is the one that was hit; a tie between a
// horizontal and a vertical face means a corner hit.
function penetrationFaces(cx, cy, r, brick) {
  const depths = [
    ['left', cx + r - brick.x],
    ['right', brick.x + brick.w - (cx - r)],
    ['top', cy + r - brick.y],
    ['bottom', brick.y + brick.h - (cy - r)],
  ];
  const min = Math.min(...depths.map(([, d]) => d));
  return depths.filter(([, d]) => d - min <= EPS).map(([name]) => name);
}

// Resolves every brick the ball touches during this step: destroys them,
// awards score, and applies EXACTLY ONE bounce (see #1). Handles the four
// failure modes of the old code:
//   - face detection via smallest penetration (per face / corner);
//   - push-out: the ball is repositioned on the face it hit, so it can never
//     overlap on the next frame and re-flip forever;
//   - neighbours: two bricks can be overlapped by the same seam — the bounce
//     is computed once, from the earliest contact, never once per brick;
//   - tunnelling: contacts are found by sweeping the segment between the
//     previous and the current position (see sweptHit).
// Returns the number of bricks destroyed (0 when the ball hits nothing).
export function resolveBrickHit(state) {
  const { ball, bricks } = state;
  const px = ball.px ?? ball.x;
  const py = ball.py ?? ball.y;

  const hits = [];
  for (const brick of bricks) {
    if (!brick.alive) continue;
    const hit = sweptHit(px, py, ball, brick);
    if (hit) hits.push({ brick, ...hit });
  }
  if (hits.length === 0) return 0;

  hits.sort((a, b) => a.t - b.t);
  const primary = hits[0];

  for (const { brick } of hits) {
    brick.alive = false;
    state.combo += 1;
    state.score += scoreForBrick(brick, state.combo);
  }

  // Single bounce, off the face of the earliest contact.
  const faces = primary.face;
  const horizontal = faces.includes('left') || faces.includes('right');
  const vertical = faces.includes('top') || faces.includes('bottom');
  if (horizontal && vertical) {
    ball.vx = -ball.vx;
    ball.vy = -ball.vy;
  } else if (vertical) {
    ball.vy = -ball.vy;
  } else if (horizontal) {
    ball.vx = -ball.vx;
  }

  // Push the ball out of the brick (no overlap left for the next frame).
  pushOut(ball, primary.brick, faces);
  return hits.length;
}

function pushOut(ball, brick, faces) {
  if (faces.includes('left')) ball.x = brick.x - ball.r;
  else if (faces.includes('right')) ball.x = brick.x + brick.w + ball.r;
  if (faces.includes('top')) ball.y = brick.y - ball.r;
  else if (faces.includes('bottom')) ball.y = brick.y + brick.h + ball.r;
}
